calls.thesis: HOLD — actively bullish and invested (8th-largest position, down ~45% in the drawdown), holding his full position into Tuesday's earnings with cautious optimism; the engagement-problem narrative is a filter that misreads everything (the Warner Bros Discovery bid, watch-time reporting, 6% / ~1,000-job layoffs), and the layoff memo reaffirmed the full-year forecast 6 days before earnings. He believes Netflix is a 25x P/E stock, not 19x.
calls.base_case: Over time Netflix proves profitable, secure, high-margin and reliable enough to rerate to a mid-20s P/E; some uncertainty is fairly priced in, but not the current narrative discount (2022 trough was ~17x).
calls.bull_case: Earnings land in line with the reaffirmed guidance and the engagement story breaks, starting the rerating from 19x towards 25x.
calls.bear_case: Near-term earnings reaction is a coin flip — a 4–7% drop is normal territory for Netflix; engagement grew only ~2% on 200B hours and he concedes the concerns are not completely invalid.

calls.video_title: Netflix Stock Down 46% Despite Record Profits. Why?
calls.thesis: HOLD (first tracked call for this creator): record profits (~$12B TTM, ~25% net margin, ROE ~50%) but at adj. P/E ~26 the -46%-from-ATH stock is fairly valued, not a bargain; he holds a small ~1% position (up ~3%) and would only add significantly much lower.
calls.base_case: Normal scenario: 14% earnings growth for 5 years then 9% (incl. ~2%/yr buybacks) → fair price ~$80; expected return ~8%.
calls.bull_case: Positive scenario: 17% then 11% growth → fair price ~50% higher, ~12%/yr return.
calls.bear_case: Negative scenario: 3% then 1% growth at a fair P/E of 11 → ~50% downside; margin expansion caps out and TV viewing share slipped 8.8%→7.8% while YouTube rose.
